title: Om Emoji 🕉️ Meaning: The Sacred Syllable of Hinduism
description: 🕉️ is Om, the sacred syllable of Hinduism, also honored in Buddhism and Jainism. See how the Om emoji is used for prayer, festivals, yoga and meditation.
summary: The 🕉️ Om emoji shows the Devanagari symbol for Om (also spelled Aum), the most sacred syllable in Hinduism, also honored in Jainism and Buddhism. Hindus use it for prayer, festivals and religious identity, while yoga and meditation communities use it for chanting, calm and spiritual practice.
meaning: For Hindus, Om is a sound and a symbol at the heart of the faith. It is chanted at the beginning and end of prayers and mantras, written on temple walls, doorways and wedding invitations, and understood in the Upanishads as expressing ultimate reality. Sending 🕉️ is therefore close to a short prayer or blessing, and in a bio it signals Hindu identity.

The emoji follows the festival calendar. It appears in greetings for Diwali, Navratri, Ganesh Chaturthi, Holi and Maha Shivratri, and in posts from temple visits and pujas at home. Many families send it with a morning "Jai Shri Ram" or "Om Namah Shivaya" message, the latter a well-known mantra to Shiva.

Outside Hinduism, Om is chanted in many Buddhist and Jain traditions, and the mantra "Om mani padme hum" is central in Tibetan Buddhism. Through yoga, the syllable also traveled into Western wellness culture: classes often begin or end with a group Om, so 🕉️ shows up on studio pages, retreat flyers and meditation playlists.

That secular adoption sits uneasily with some Hindus, who see the symbol used as decoration on mats, clothes or tattoos without understanding. Using 🕉️ with awareness of its sacred meaning avoids that problem. In Hindu homes the symbol is treated with reverence, kept away from the floor and from shoes, and many users carry that care over to how and where they post it.

contexts.label: On Hindu festivals
contexts.body: Diwali, Navratri, Durga Puja, Ganesh Chaturthi and Shivratri greetings often include 🕉️ with 🪔 lamps or 🙏. Families share it in group chats with images of deities and blessings for the day. Temples and cultural associations add it to event announcements and livestreams of aarti.

contexts.label: In yoga and meditation
contexts.body: Studios, teachers and practitioners use 🕉️ for chanting, breathwork and a calm, centered mood. It often sits beside 🧘 and ☮️ in captions. Many teachers mention its roots in Hindu tradition; some practitioners, especially Hindus, ask that it not be used as a mere aesthetic.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Among Hindu friends and family, 🕉️ works as a blessing at the start or end of a message, a way to say good morning with a spiritual note, or a reply to news of a puja or pilgrimage. It is warm and respectful, never jokey.

examples.text: Happy Diwali to you and your family 🕉️🪔
examples.meaning: A festival greeting wishing light and blessings.

examples.text: Om Namah Shivaya 🕉️ good morning everyone
examples.meaning: A morning message invoking Shiva, common in family group chats.

examples.text: Class ends with three Oms tonight, come early 🕉️🧘
examples.meaning: A yoga teacher describing the closing chant.

examples.text: Back from the temple, feeling peaceful 🕉️
examples.meaning: The sender visited a Hindu temple for prayer.

examples.text: Grihapravesh puja on Sunday, please join us 🕉️🙏
examples.meaning: An invitation to a housewarming ceremony with Hindu prayers.

combos.meaning: Prayer and reverence; a blessing or greeting.
Diwali and other festivals of lamps.
Offerings at puja; flowers placed before a deity.

confusedWith.difference: ☸️ is the dharma wheel, primarily a Buddhist symbol of the Buddha's teaching. 🕉️ is the sacred syllable Om, central to Hinduism and used in Buddhism and Jainism as a chant.
🪔 is a small oil lamp, the diya lit for Diwali and puja. It marks a festival or an act of worship, while 🕉️ is the symbol of the sacred sound itself.
🛕 shows a temple building and refers to visiting or worshiping there. 🕉️ is abstract and can be used anywhere, from prayers to greetings.

avoid: Do not use 🕉️ as a random decorative swirl or a stand-in for the number 3.
Avoid pairing it with alcohol, partying or crude jokes; many Hindus find that disrespectful.
design: The Devanagari Om glyph: a figure like a curled 3 with a tail, topped by a crescent and a dot (the chandrabindu). Most platforms draw it in white on the purple religious-symbol tile. Some text fonts show it as a plain black character. The shape follows standard Devanagari calligraphy and is consistent across vendors.

faqs.q: Is the Om emoji Hindu or Buddhist?
faqs.a: Om is most closely associated with Hinduism, and the glyph is written in Devanagari script. Buddhists and Jains also chant Om in their own traditions, so the syllable is shared, but the emoji is generally read as a Hindu symbol.

Yoga developed within Indian religious traditions, and many classes chant Om at the start or end. The emoji marks that practice and a meditative mood. Respectful teachers also acknowledge its sacred meaning.

faqs.q: Is it disrespectful to use 🕉️ if I'm not Hindu?
faqs.a: Not if it is used with respect, such as festival greetings or yoga practice that honors its roots. Using it as fashion or decoration, or next to alcohol or crude jokes, can offend.

faqs.q: What does 🕉️ mean in a bio?
faqs.a: Usually that the person is Hindu or follows a dharmic spiritual practice. It can also mark a yoga teacher or meditation account, so the rest of the profile tells you which.

faqs.q: When was the Om emoji added?
faqs.a: Om was added to Unicode in 2014 and is listed under Emoji 0.7, together with other religious symbols such as ☸️ and ☪️.
